clue.text: One has an excess of trouble and strife

definitions.text: One has an excess of trouble and strife

parts.words: One has an excess of trouble and strife
parts.note: trouble and strife is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, so this describes someone with more than one spouse at a time

explanation.surface: Someone who has far too many problems and arguments in their life.
explanation.walkthrough: Trouble and strife is Cockney rhyming slang (a London dialect) for wife; an excess of wives means being married to several at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with more than one wife at the same time practises polygamy, the cryptic reading of the clue.

clue.text: East European boom?

definitions.meaning: a native of Poland, in Eastern Europe
a boom is a long spar or ..., as on a sailing boat or a microphone

explanation.definitionFit: A Pole comes from Poland in Eastern Europe, and a boom is a long rigid spar or rod.

clue.text: Devil is cruel if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A remark that the devil is cruel when he is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns CRUEL and IF into a new order; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is one of the traditional names for Satan, the fallen angel.

clue.text: Enjoying good food almost organic in production

indicators.note: in production suggests the letters are being worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Food that is very nearly organic being made for gourmets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in production' rearranges ALMOST and ORGANIC, all thirteen letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomical describes gastronomy, the art and pleasure of eating fine food.

clue.text: Party with disguise representing queen in Middle East

indicators.note: in places the letters for representing and queen inside the abbreviation for Middle East

parts.note: as means representing, playing the part of

explanation.surface: A costume party where a guest dresses as a queen in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' gives AS, as in playing a part; QU for queen is less familiar than R or ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A masque was a courtly entertainment, and a masquerade party is one where guests wear masks.

clue.text: Merlin perhaps turns up something of a treasure re crosswords

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wizard produces something to do with a cherished crossword collection.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turns up' means read upwards: RERECROS, read from the bottom, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is the wizard of Arthurian legend, an example of a magician.

clue.text: Was enigmatic Becket initially something absorbing in theatre?

indicators.note: enigmatic, puzzling, means the letters of the preceding word are jumbled
initially means take just the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A question about whether the playwright Beckett was being cryptic in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is an operating theatre, not a playhouse, despite the dramatist named in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a pad of absorbent material used to mop up blood during surgery.

clue.text: Done in with two journalists

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, the first of the pair
ED, the editor, is the second journalist

explanation.surface: Being killed off in company with a pair of reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two journalists' gives both a hack and an editor (ED).
explanation.definitionFit: Done in, exhausted, is British slang matched by whacked, meaning worn out.

clue.text: One may call wife so fat her belt is tight

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A man calling his wife fat because her belt is too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is tight' means drunk here, signalling FAT HER BELT rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is an affectionate idiom for one's spouse, especially a wife.

clue.text: Place before Eliot possible producers of the Waste Land

definitions.text: possible producers of the Waste Land

indicators.note: before puts the place in front of the poet's initials

parts.note: locus means a place or position
T. S. Eliot, the poet, gives his initials

explanation.surface: A literary note setting a location ahead of Eliot's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Waste Land is Eliot's poem, but here a swarm leaves a wasteland behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of locusts strip crops and leave devastated, barren land behind them.

clue.text: Ruling in the club when prince is absent

indicators.note: is absent says a letter is missing from the word before

parts.note: in the club is British slang for pregnant

explanation.surface: A royal ruling made at the club while the prince is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, not a social club; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant who rules in her own right.

clue.text: International conflict with Chinese rulers once a major threat

parts.note: global means worldwide, international
war is a conflict
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A warning that a worldwide war involving former Chinese emperors would be catastrophic.
explanation.definitionFit: Global warming, the rise in world temperatures, is widely seen as a grave danger.

clue.text: It contains advice to the benefit of batsman that is about to prepare for playing

parts.note: for means on behalf of, to the benefit of
to tune an instrument is to get it ready for playing
Alastair Cook was an England batsman
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Tips for a cricketer who is about to get ready to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Cook was an England cricket opener; 'about' places TUNE ahead of COOK IE, as a loose positional link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune cookie is a crisp biscuit holding a slip of paper with a prediction or advice.

clue.text: Old form of transport for men good for the environment reduced pain

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
eco means environmentally friendly

indicators.note: reduced means the word for pain is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A green, painless old transport system for men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' clips ACHE to ACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach was a horse-drawn coach running between stages on a regular route.

clue.text: Codebreaker switching sides heartlessly

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: turning, as in turning traitor, means switching sides

explanation.surface: A spy who changes allegiance without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning means switching sides, as a double agent does; 'heartlessly' drops its middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing led codebreaking work on the Enigma cipher at Bletchley Park in the Second World War.

clue.text: Husband follows Queen in museum gallery

indicators.note: follows places the husband's letter after the rest
in puts the queen's letters inside the museum's abbreviation

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A husband trailing the Queen around a gallery of a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; ER goes inside V AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: A verandah is a roofed open gallery or porch along the outside of a house.

clue.text: Part of church making intricate patterns

indicators.note: making intricate means the letters are woven into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A section of a church decorated with elaborate designs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making intricate' rearranges PATTERNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of the cross-shaped floor plan of a church.

clue.text: French lady among foreign girls sheds little light

indicators.note: among places the French lady inside the other letters
foreign suggests the letters are made strange and rearranged

parts.note: MME is the abbreviation for Madame

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman in a group of overseas girls gives off a faint glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges the girls, and the French lady sits within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Glimmers are faint, wavering lights, so it gives off only a little light.

clue.text: I am set in position enforced by authority

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
posed means placed or arranged in position, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone complaining they have been placed somewhere by official order.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule imposed is one forced on people by those in power.

clue.text: Short wave broadcast live turn

parts.note: SW is the abbreviation for short wave

indicators.note: broadcast, scattered about, means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio programme on short wave going out live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges LIVE to IVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn or rotate about a fixed point.

clue.text: Performing on vocal my output is hot stuff

indicators.note: performing means the letters are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer boasting that their vocal performance is sensational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges ON VOCAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano speaks of its output, molten lava, which is literally hot stuff.

clue.text: Get too much as composer endlessly rings out

indicators.note: out, as in outside, puts the rings around the shortened composer

parts.note: two rings are two letter O shapes

indicators.note: endlessly means the composer loses his last letter

parts.note: Verdi was an Italian composer

explanation.surface: Taking too much while the composer's music rings out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' works as outside here; 'as' is a link, and 'Get too much' means take too much of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take or do it to excess, having too much.

clue.text: Place to launch a nut say in California

indicators.note: in puts the nut and the saying inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: a pecan is a nut
aver means to say or declare

explanation.surface: A suggestion of where to throw a nut in California.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests throwing a nut; the place is the Florida spaceport, and California's abbreviation is split around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral in Florida is the site of NASA's main rocket launch facilities.

clue.text: Metal to conduct

definitions.meaning: a heavy grey metal, chemical symbol Pb
to guide or direct, as a conductor ... an orchestra

explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a soft heavy metal, and to lead is to conduct or guide.

clue.text: Excuse sailor needs to finish crossword?

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
to solve a crossword is to complete it

explanation.surface: A seaman explaining why he must complete his puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to excuse someone, freeing them from blame or guilt.

clue.text: Surrey town to send down one ousting the French

indicators.note: ousting means one piece pushes another out and takes its place

parts.note: to relegate is to send down, as a football team to a lower division
le is French for the
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Surrey town demoting someone by expelling the French.
explanation.walkthrough: Reigate is a town in Surrey, a county south of London; I replaces LE in RELEGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a market town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: Leather cover

definitions.meaning: an animal skin used for leather
to conceal, or a shelter for watching birds

explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin made into leather, and to hide is to cover or conceal.

clue.text: Keep firm grip

parts.note: strong means firm and sturdy
a hold is a grip

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a tight grasp on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' is the noun, the fortified tower of a castle, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the central fortified tower of a castle, a stronghold.
